purpose: Reconstruct the actual terminal preparation curve on the Wuhan-Hankou -> Yueyang/Pailiuchi axis without assuming a May launch date, then identify the earliest date on which the staged Hunan operation has a robust force/logistics/engineer/air gate.

method.rule: Use branch-fixed OOB and terminal totals as end constraints, reconstruct monotonic dated bands from force location, transport/repair clocks, Nanjing substitution and plausible river/rail accumulation; charge Allied detection/interdiction rather than assume perfect concealment.
historical_sanity: Historical Ichi-Go preparations were ordered in January 1944; March saw organization of independent brigades and air maintenance/supply units.
Historical Japanese planning relied heavily on inland water transport and rapid rail repair because gasoline and shipping were constrained.
Historical Fourteenth Air Force attacks did not prevent Japanese accumulation at Hankow; much Yangtze movement was at night and used defended ports.

fixed_hunan_package.note: Seven of the ten Hunan divisions are already 11th-Army-area formations in the January baseline; 27th/37th have months to rebuild/redeploy after Five-Go; 64th is enabled to move from lower Yangtze by Nanjing rear substitution. Unit arrival is therefore not the terminal pacing item.

weekly.chinese_detection: LOW_MEDIUM: local troop/rail/river activity visible, operation scale not yet separable from routine reinforcement.
MEDIUM: heavy Yangtze movement and support-unit concentration increasingly inconsistent with routine garrison rotation.
MEDIUM_HIGH: Changsha/Hunan becomes a credible major-objective hypothesis, but exact H-hour and force scale remain uncertain.
HIGH on a spring Hunan operation; exact start remains poorly fixed because most core divisions are long-standing 11th Army formations.
HIGH: broad intent likely known; Chinese/US response shifts from discovering the operation to delaying its logistics and preserving field forces.
VERY_HIGH: analogous to Chennault 19-Apr historical assessment that major Yangtze movement made a Changsha offensive virtually certain. Branch exact date still hidden.
VERY_HIGH intent / LOW exact H-hour. Japanese terminal gate is robustly crossed.

weekly.note: Counterfactual continuation only, supplied to reconcile the prior early-May 175-225kt terminal total. Actual branch launches before this date, so use the opening-operation ledger for 30-Apr remaining stocks.

prelaunch_interdiction_charge_1944-03-15.route_effect: Periodic daytime barge/rail/road disruption and local bridge/yard damage; no sustained break of Wuhan-Hankow -> Yueyang system because night river movement, defended ports, dispersal and repair absorb the attacks.
prelaunch_interdiction_charge_1944-03-15.anti_double_count: These are terminal-preparation working charges embedded in the weekly net stocks/serviceability; do not debit them again.

gate_crossing.force_concentration: PASS by 1944-04-12; not pacing after that.
gate_crossing.vehicle_serviceability: PASS robustly by 1944-04-19 and reaches the prior 5.4-6.5k launch band by 1944-04-26.
gate_crossing.forward_stock: ROBUST PASS 1944-04-26 when lower-band immediate draw reaches 50kt and campaign stock exceeds 160kt.
gate_crossing.air_support: PASS by 1944-04-19..26; 175-205 aircraft-class short surge can be generated without terminating western pressure.
gate_crossing.why_not_earlier: A six-division limited attack is possible earlier, but the approved staged ten-division scheme would accept too little ammunition/POL/bridge reserve and too much risk of a 14AF-induced pause before the Changsha logistics nodes are reached.
